title: Workload cartography & SLA playbook — Veridian Aviation POC kickoff
summary: Kickoff for a POC to validate inference footprint, tail-latency behavior under bursty booking traffic, and gating criteria for Dedicated vs Private deployment. Agreed on success metrics (95th and 99th latencies, cost per 1k requests), replay/baseline benchmarks, and a three-week timeline for initial runbook and results.
action_items: Carlos Reyes | Share synthetic traffic logs (1 month) + sample inference traces | 2028-12-09
Ethan Park | Produce initial benchmark harness and runner script (k6 + replay adapter) | 2028-12-12
Dr. Anika Shah | Provide 10 canonical prompts and failure cases for quality gating | 2028-12-10
Maya Thompson | Send pricing deck and Dedicated sizing estimate | 2028-12-08
Priya Menon | Confirm VPC connectivity constraints and egress rules | 2028-12-11
next_steps: Redwood to ingest customer's week-of-traffic CSV and run a 24h synthetic replay to estimate tail-latency.
Customer to review the proposed success criteria doc and mark any regulatory gating items.
Schedule two-hour benchmark run next Friday (12/15) to test quantized vs fp16 variants.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue 2028-12-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), Carlos (Veridian Head of Platform), Anika (ML Lead), Priya (SRE), Tom (Procurement)

Summary (auto): kickoff to scope workload cartography and POC success metrics, focus on bursts from booking windows and long tail of response length.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have most folks. Quick note, we're recording this, we'll send the deck and the benchmark template after.
[00:14] Carlos: Yep thanks. We're excited, been wanting to size this properly before we commit to the dedicated pools. Our main fear is the two-minute booking window where we see a huge spike.
[00:28] Ethan: Cool. Can you give us rough numbers on that spike, like QPS and concurrency?
[00:35] Carlos: Uh, so normal is around 12 QPS average across the day. During the booking window we see short bursts up to — it's noisy — maybe 180 QPS sustained for 90 to 120 seconds, and then a decaying tail.
[00:52] Anika: And those requests vary a lot in length; the flight re-pricing prompts are short, like 20 to 60 tokens in, but the responses can be pretty long because we generate step-by-step itinerary text, average output ~320 tokens, some go to 800+ on rare itineraries.
[01:12] Priya: Also, existing infra has about 600 concurrent connections during peak but many are idle waiting for token streams, so we want to understand connection pooling and websocket behavior.
[01:29] Ethan: That helps. For the POC we typically ask for a traffic sample — CSV of timestamps, input token counts, output token counts, and any metadata like cached prompt IDs. That lets us build a replay and map QPS->token throughput.
[01:49] Carlos: We'll share a month of anonymized logs. Expect a couple of hiccups in schema, hope that's okay.
[01:56] Maya: Totally fine. On success criteria, propose we gate on three pillars: (1) Latency: 95th < 450ms for short responses (<128 out tokens) and 95th < 1.2s for long responses, (2) Cost: under $X per 1k requests — we'll put a number in the deck, (3) Quality: no more than 2% regression on the canonical prompt set. Thoughts?
[02:24] Anika: The latency buckets sound reasonable but we need a 99th percentile check too, our users are very sensitive — maybe 99th < 2.5s for long responses.
[02:34] Maya: Yep we can add that. Note that tail latency will depend on model and whether we use prefix KV cash — I mean KV cache — sorry, the auto prefix caching.
[02:46] Ethan: Quick technical aside: our runtime supports continuous batching and can autotune batch windows to meet SLOs; however, high burst QPS means you might need reserved concurrency or Dedicated pools to avoid cold-start tails.
[03:02] Priya: Are there examples of similar customers? How did they size Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:09] Maya: We had an internal retail customer with 150 QPS bursts; they used Reserved Dedicated with a small buffer and autoscale policy with pre-warmed nodes. Cost tradeoff was about 30% higher than pure hosted but much more predictable tail latency.
[03:27] Tom: From procurement perspective we care about predictable monthly commit and an option to failover to hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[03:36] Ethan: We can propose a hybrid routing policy: primary to Dedicated in-region, fallback to hosted (lower-tier model) in another region if capacity is limited; that'll keep availability up but may change output characteristics. We'll flag differences in model variants for your QA.
[03:56] Anika: On model variants — can you run comparisons between fp16, int8 quantized, and 4-bit quant? We care about quality drop vs cost savings.
[04:07] Ethan: Yes, part of the benchmark plan: we'll run three variants: fp16 (baseline), q8_0 style quantized, and q4_0 micro-quant. We'll compute average embedding/cross-entropy drift on your canonical prompts and measure hallucination rates on the failure set.
[04:24] Carlos: Hallucinations are the real showstopper for us. We need a quality gating step before any auto-rollout.
[04:31] Lina: We'll include a regression alert in Redwood Optimize; we can wire your evals so any metric beyond threshold pauses rollouts.
[04:39] Maya: Great. Back to traffic shape — Anika you said outputs average 320 tokens but distribution heavy tail. Do you have percentiles?
[04:49] Anika: Roughly: median output 210, 75th 380, 95th 620, 99th 920. Inputs median 35, 95th 120. There are a lot of multipart itineraries that bump the tail.
[05:05] Ethan: Perfect. That's the data we need to compute tokens-per-second under burst. For example, 180 QPS * avg output 320 tokens = 57,600 output tokens per second, which affects both GPU memory and throughput planning.
[05:22] Priya: Also note we have regulatory requirements to keep PII out of logs; we'll sanitize before sharing.
[05:28] Maya: Understood. For the POC plan timeline, suggest week 0: ingest logs and align success criteria; week 1: baseline replay run (fp16); week 2: quantized runs + canary routing tests; week 3: compile results and hand-off. Does that timeline work?
[05:46] Carlos: That's aggressive but fine. We want the 24h synthetic replay by week 1 so we can see tail spikes.
[05:54] Ethan: For the replay we'll create a k6 script that replays timestamps scaled to desired QPS. We'll also add jitter to mimic real bursts. We'll push the harness to your sandbox repo and run together.
[06:07] Anika: For the quality evals, we'll need a human-in-the-loop sample set. Can Redwood support annotation pipelines?
[06:15] Lina: Yes, we have a lightweight eval runner and a UI for quick annotations; we can export CSVs for your team.
[06:22] Tom: Licensing & procurement question — if Dedicated is needed, what's the minimum commit?
[06:29] Maya: Typical min monthly for Dedicated starts at three reserved GPU nodes for an annual purchase; we'll send a sizing note with cost bands. For the POC we can use hosted or trial Dedicated credits.
[06:40] Tom: Okay, and SLA — what's the expected uptime? We need enterprise SLA language for review.
[06:47] Maya: We'll attach our SLA summary and SOC 2 attestation in the follow-up packet.
[06:53] Carlos: One other nuance: our edge caching layer occasionally serves stale prompts; we'll include TTL rules in the logs so you can simulate cache hits.
[07:02] Ethan: Good call. Cache-hit ratio changes effective load a lot. If you see 40% prefix cache hits, effective token generation drops.
[07:12] Anika: Also we have batch post-processing that concatenates outputs for downstream indexing — sometimes that inflates observed token counts in logs. We'll flag those rows.
[07:24] Maya: Great. I'll propose success thresholds in a doc: latency buckets, cost target, and <2% quality drift. We'll email that and request sign-off before we run the live replay.
[07:36] Carlos: Sign-off process: engineering approves latency and topology, legal approves data sharing, procurement approves limited trial commit. Should be doable by next Friday.
[07:46] Priya: From an SRE standpoint, we want guidance on connection pooling: recommended max inflight per connection and websocket keepalive windows.
[07:56] Ethan: We'll provide recommendations: keep max inflight per connection at 8-12 depending on average response length; use 30s keepalives and a per-connection throughput cap to avoid head-of-line blocking. We'll add concrete numbers in the runbook.
[08:12] Anika: For benchmarks, please include both token-limited and time-limited runs. Token-limited to stress throughput, time-limited to stress tail behavior.
[08:21] Ethan: Noted. We'll design the suite: 1) 24h scaled replay, 2) 2 x 5m sustained burst at 180 QPS, 3) 30 x short-burst spikes of 10–20s to emulate booking windows.
[08:36] Maya: We'll also test fallback routing: Dedicated primary -> hosted fallback with model-variant changes. We'll measure quality delta and latencies for fallback.
[08:47] Carlos: That fallback data is critical for us to accept a hybrid routing approach.
[08:52] Tom: Procurement needs the POC scope doc and terms. Maya you'll send that?
[08:57] Maya: Yes, I'll send a POC scope + T&Cs.
[09:01] Anika: One small ask: can we run a cheap, early smoke test that uses just 10 minutes of sampled traffic to verify connectivity and basic throughput?
[09:09] Ethan: Absolutely. We typically do a smoke run to validate connectivity and then the full replay. We'll coordinate exact times with Priya.
[09:18] Priya: We can open a temporary VPC peering session and provide IP allowlist for Redwood test nodes. We'll get that to Maya by Monday.
[09:27] Maya: Awesome. I'll enumerate required firewall rules in the follow-up email.
[09:33] Lina: For the quality gating, we'll attach the eval job to the rollout pipeline so if your canonical prompt set fails, automatic rollback is triggered.
[09:41] Anika: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:44] Carlos: One last thing — in the report, include a modeled cost projection for 3 scenarios: mostly-hosted (no reserved), hybrid with 20% Dedicated, and full Dedicated. We need that for our 2029 budget planning.
[09:58] Maya: We'll include cost bands and assumptions.
[10:02] Tom: Great. Then next steps?
[10:04] Maya: Recap: Carlos shares logs by Friday, Redwood sends POC scope + pricing and runner scripts by Monday, team executes smoke test early next week, and full benchmark next Friday.
[10:18] Carlos: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[10:21] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links: POC scope doc, benchmark runner repo, and a spreadsheet template for traffic.
